title: South Island Atlas
outcome: Christchurch as the hub of a connected South Island, with a rail plan to start on
summary: An interactive atlas that makes the case for connected transport in Greater Christchurch, with the city as the hub of the South Island. A ten-page story sets out what is already built and what is planned. The plan starts with commuter trains from Rolleston and Rangiora on the existing track, ending at Pilgrim Place for the 2027 trial, then growing into an all-day service. The history view traces the South Island's lines in use today and the branch lines and tramways that came before them. It began as the Canterbury Rail Atlas.

sections.head: A debate spread across a dozen reports
sections.body: Passenger rail in Christchurch has been studied, voted on and promised for years, from Aurecon's 2014 assessment to ECan's business case vote in 2025 and a commuter trial due in 2027. The evidence sits in separate reports and datasets, and none of them shows the track, the land, the people and the buses together.

sections.head: Start on the track that exists
sections.body: Put the existing infrastructure on one map, then draw a plan that could start soon and grow: a peak-hour pilot on KiwiRail's track, stations where the bus and MRT networks meet the rail, and an honest look at what the first central stop can and can't do.

sections.head: An atlas with a plan in it
sections.body: The atlas has views for the region, history, public land, industry, track, buses and traffic, stations, Pilgrim Place, alternatives and infrastructure. The alternatives view sketches a trench under Manchester St to a station at Tuam St, a block from the Bus Interchange and the stadium. The infrastructure view, built on Christchurch City Council's open datasets, is moving to live council data, and the history view traces every South Island branch line with its stations and junctions. The existing infrastructure comes from council, ECan, KiwiRail and LINZ open data; the plan, the regional and historic layers and the writing are mine.
